acme_prod_owner: Hey team — we're getting consistent 413s from the embeddings endpoint when sending large batches via our streaming/chunked uploader. Happens around 9-11MB per chunk. Started yesterday after we switched to a client-side chunker to avoid timeouts.

acme_prod_owner: Error snippet from our client: `HTTP/1.1 413 Request Entity Too Large`

acme_prod_owner: Using Redwood SDK v2.1.0, endpoint `/v1/embeddings/batch` with Content-Type: application/json and Transfer-Encoding: chunked. Payload looks like: `[ {"id": "...", "text": "..."}, ... ]` per chunk.

sara_support: sorry you're running into this — can you paste the exact curl or python request you use for a chunk so we can repro? Also which model / embedding dimension are you targeting? :eyes:

acme_prod_owner: here's a minimal repro (python):

```python
import requests
url = "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings/batch"
headers = {"Authorization": "Bearer xxxx", "Content-Type": "application/json"}
chunks = [big_json_chunk1, big_json_chunk2]
for c in chunks:
    r = requests.post(url, data=c, headers=headers)
    print(r.status_code, r.text)
```

acme_prod_owner: We target `redwood-embed-768` (expected dim 768). Each item ~ 2.5KB average, ~4k items per chunk.

michael_eng: thanks. 413 usually means a gateway/nginx/body-size limit, not a dimensional mismatch. A few things to check:
- whether your client sends `Content-Length` per request or chunked transfer (some proxies treat chunked oddly)
- upstream API gateway has a per-request max payload (we default to 8MB config)
- any CDN/LB in front of us that could cut this off

michael_eng: can you try one of two quick tests: (1) reduce chunk to 4k -> smaller than observed failure point, (2) send same payload with explicit Content-Length header (no Transfer-Encoding: chunked) and see if it behaves differently?

acme_prod_owner: I tried smaller chunks and 4k still fails. At ~2k items (~5MB) it succeeds. Also we tried setting Content-Length and it still 413s when payload > ~8.5MB.

raj_reliability: pinging infra — we had a recent change to the ingress controller that enforces `client_max_body_size` at 8MB for some internal routes. I will trace for the embeddings route specifically. @michael_eng any chance the embeddings service runs behind a separate proxy config?

michael_eng: embeddings runs behind the shared api-gateway v2; the route should respect higher limits but can be overridden per route. I'll dump the route config.

upload-bot: [automation] Received ticket #SUP-9182: "embeddings 413 on chunked upload" assigned to sara_support, michael_eng.

sara_support: Thanks. acme, can you share request/response headers from a failed request (redact tokens)? We specifically want `Content-Type`, `Content-Length`, `Transfer-Encoding`, `Via`, and any `x-forwarded-*` headers.

acme_prod_owner: pasted below (redacted):
```
Request headers:
Authorization: Bearer [REDACTED]
Content-Type: application/json
Transfer-Encoding: chunked
User-Agent: acme-uploader/1.2

Response headers:
Server: nginx
Date: Mon, 02 Mar 2026 14:12:11 GMT
Content-Length: 18
Connection: close
```

acme_prod_owner: Note `Server: nginx` on the response, even though we expected our gateway to hide that.

raj_reliability: that suggests the gateway/nginx is terminating and returning 413. I found a route override for `/v1/embeddings/batch` where `client_max_body_size` was mistakenly set to `8m` after a recent deploy. Rolling back in 5m.

acme_prod_owner: thanks. Any ETA? This is affecting nightly ingestion jobs.

raj_reliability: rolling back now — applying config and reloading. Should be quick, but in the meantime you can reduce chunk size to ~5MB or use smaller concurrent workers as a workaround.

michael_eng: also a note on dimension mismatches — sometimes customers get 400 errors when embedding dim doesn't match model expectations. If you see a 400 with `dimension_mismatch` we have a different plan. This thread is 413-specific.

sara_support: while we're rolling, would you be able to try gzip compression? Sending compressed JSON can often keep payloads under the limit. Add header `Content-Encoding: gzip` and compress the body. It tends to reduce size significantly for textual data.

acme_prod_owner: good idea — trying gzip now.

acme_prod_owner: ok gzip + 9MB raw compressed to 3.4MB and request succeeded. Thanks, that confirms the limit.

raj_reliability: rollback complete. Can you retry uncompressed?

acme_prod_owner: retrying uncompressed now... got 200 OK for same chunk that previously 413ed. Looks good.

acme_prod_owner: follow-ups/questions: 1) will this limit be documented? 2) any recommended chunk sizes we should standardize on?

sara_support: yes — we'll add a note to the embeddings docs about pragmatic per-request size guidance and chunking patterns (recommend <6MB per request uncompressed, or gzip when sending larger). Also include an example streaming uploader snippet.

michael_eng: recommendation from eng: target <=5MB uncompressed per request for best reliability across regions and customers unless you arrange dedicated routing. If you need higher throughput, we can discuss a dedicated ingest endpoint (Reserved capacity / Dedicated package) or a signed S3 ingestion flow.

jen_billing: tagging billing because customers sometimes hit extra ingress costs with retries; if they switch to gzip it might reduce egress but increase CPU usage - fine to mention tradeoffs.

acme_prod_owner: appreciated. One more: we're seeing intermittent 400s with `dimension_mismatch` on some old items during replay. Any fast tips?

michael_eng: quick check: verify your stored vector dim matches the model. If you replay items created with a different model, you'll get a mismatch when attempting to re-index or compare. If you need, provide a sample id and we can inspect.

acme_prod_owner: will gather a sample and open a separate thread for the dimension issue. For this ticket, gzip + rollback fixed it. Thanks all :tada:

sara_support: great — closing SUP-9182 after we update docs. If you want an ingest best-practices doc sooner, I can DM a checklist.

upload-bot: [automation] Ticket SUP-9182 status -> resolved by raj_reliability.
